rubric.assembly: Statuses and decisions explicitly authored after semantic review of each question. Code only assembles exact excerpts/line citations and checks structure; no keyword or automated pass grading.
rubric.observed_quotes: Repeated full current-answer quotes preserve context and show no cross-answer borrowing. Deficiency cases have narrower exact excerpts.

borderline_key_scope_concerns.detail: The index specifically requires return of a spent X-token. The literal “what can X-tokens do” is less explicit about disposal, but the use procedure includes it; retained as required rather than silently relaxing the index. Movement need not separately enumerate slot 5 because the given algorithm excludes it.
The numerically reversed mapping is substantive, even though the preceding generic range definition is right.
Per-icon discount resolves double-icon arithmetic and the ordered pay-before-resolve procedure resolves up-front cost; do not demand duplicate negative wording.
Acquisition reputation is a track reward. Counting it as a zoo icon is a false extra rule, not merely omission.
“Player-count limit” identifies a dependency but does not individually give the cap equal to the player count. No inference from other answers was used.
Explicit identification of printed standard size as the category determinant resolves actual tile/capacity exclusion without repeating a negative sentence.
Correct substitute wording coexists with an express refusal to settle the actual quantity-limit question; cannot pass merely because the support label is ignored.

Index embeds “into hand” in its first part. The literal question asks where cards come from and where later played, not their intermediate destination. Answer resolves the actual source and later destination. This is an explicit scope dispute, not a change to the factual key.
The question asks the flock/release interaction, so “normal release procedure” can refer to the defined release/fallback procedure. No details are borrowed from the reader’s Q17.
The question asks how the two actions are resolved. The answer describes a chosen multiplied use; it does not clearly assert compulsory spending of every Multiplier.
The fee sentence lacks the otherwise/no-token-removed condition. Do not silently append the condition because an earlier sentence states the exemption.
“Its owner” refers to the named Science Library subject; no explicit wrong player is assigned.
Connected/isolated are game terms defined in the same frozen summary; the answer uses both consistently, without claiming connected terrain regions suffice.

“Under normal rules” is an ordinary default for placing the named unique building rather than a separate placement-exception demand in this literal question. Answer requires placement and claims no exemption. Own-zoo is the Sponsor-reference default, not an all-player trigger.
Question requests Hunter X interaction and duplicate icon behavior, not the entire Hunter definition or rock adjacency; index appropriately classifies those as context.
“Per group of six ... evaluating each group separately” means complete sixes within each contiguous group, not pooling remainders; no worked arithmetic example is requested.
Self-target outcomes are absent. Duplicate leader is ambiguous in the word “separately”; an explicit twice-from-same-zoo result appears elsewhere but was not borrowed.
Unlike Q21, all literal parts are explicitly resolved. A separate reordering choice is denied consistently with the mandatory keep-order rule. The reader’s partial label is not a grading verdict.

Index requires a separate multi-building sequencing statement. Literal question asks about one standard enclosure’s face and when/how often its covered placement bonuses are gained. “Each ... immediately once when covered” resolves that actual request. Inter-building sequencing remains source-correct context, flagged explicitly rather than silently overriding the index.

key_concerns: No factual key was revised. Broader key context was not independently demanded. Literal-question/index scope concerns are listed explicitly.

summarysupportquote.quote: **X-tokens.** You may use X-tokens to increase an action's strength: each token spent adds +1 strength, then returns to the supply. You may spend any number in one action (for some actions, strength above 5 no longer improves the action). You can never hold more than 5 X-tokens. You must pay each item before receiving its own benefits. You set the strength **before** performing the action — X-tokens gained while performing an action cannot boost that same action.

judgments.question: Can money or other bonuses gained during an action pay for a later building, animal or association task in that action? How do immediate and after-finishing effects and simultaneous effects differ?

requestedparts.part: Earlier action money and other bonuses may fund later items
requestedparts.observedquote: Bonuses gained earlier in an action, including money, cards and newly activated workers, can be used in later steps of that same action. Pay each item before receiving that item's own benefit, and an animal's full cost must be payable before its money-gain effect pays out. Immediate effects resolve as they occur; ‘after finishing’ effects wait until the whole action and Action-card movement are complete. If effects are simultaneous, the owning player chooses their order.

judgments.question: Give the four Association task strengths, side-I/II task limits, worker requirements when repeating a task before a break, and whether other players workers matter.

requestedparts.part: Task strengths are reputation two, partner three, university four and conservation five
requestedparts.observedquote: The four Association tasks have strengths: increase reputation 2, gain a partner zoo 3, gain a university 4, and conservation project work 5. Association I performs exactly one task. Association II may perform one or more different tasks whose total strength is at most the action strength. A task requires one active worker; if one of your workers is already on that task, place two workers for another use; if three are already there, it cannot be repeated before the break. Workers of other players do not affect this limit.
requestedparts.observedquote_scope: current answer only; complete answer quoted where no narrower deficiency excerpt is needed

summarysupportquote.quote: - **Increase reputation (strength 2):** increase your zoo's reputation by **2**, taking any track bonuses you reach.

- **Gain partner zoo (strength 3):** take a partner zoo from the Association board onto the lowest empty partner-zoo space of your map (take any printed bonus immediately). All your partner zoos must be from different continents, maximum 4 total; the third (or fourth) requires the upgraded Association action. If every zoo currently on the board is one you already have, or you cannot place it, you cannot perform this task. Each partner zoo reduces the cost of Animal cards from its continent by 3 money per continent icon, provides 1 icon of that continent (usable for card effects and conservation projects), and some Animal cards require one.

- **Gain university (strength 4):** take a university from the Association board onto the lowest available university space and take its covered-space bonus immediately. **Also gain the reputation printed on the university tile immediately.** You cannot take a duplicate university. Universities grant reputation and research icons and are the only way to increase your hand limit to 5.

- **Conservation project work (strength 5):** either support a conservation project already in play, or play a Conservation Project card from your hand and support it immediately. A new card goes on the leftmost space above the Association board, pushing existing cards one place right. Depending on player count there can only be up to 2, 3, or 4 cards above the board (e.g., 3 with three players); if the new card exceeds the limit, discard the rightmost card and return any player tokens on it to their owners' supplies (not to their zoo maps). **The Base Conservation Projects below the board never move and are never replenished**, even when fully supported.

judgments.question: Where do partner zoos and universities come from and go, can duplicates be acquired, how are bonuses handled, and what are partner and hand-limit restrictions?

requestedparts.part: Take available tiles from the Association board
requestedparts.observedquote: Partner zoos and universities are taken from available tiles on the Association board and placed on the lowest empty space in the corresponding column of your map; take any covered-space bonus immediately, and university reputation immediately. You cannot take a duplicate university or partner zoos from a continent you already have; the zoo limit is four and the third/fourth require Association II. Partners/universities are restocked at breaks with one tile of each kind, except kinds already owned by every player, and no duplicate available tiles are added. The hand-limit university raises your break hand limit from 3 to 5; other universities do not change it. University research/reputation icons and partner continent icons count as zoo icons.

summarysupportquote.quote: - **Gain partner zoo (strength 3):** take a partner zoo from the Association board onto the lowest empty partner-zoo space of your map (take any printed bonus immediately). If every zoo currently on the board is one you already have, or you cannot place it, you cannot perform this task. judgments.question: How may a Conservation Project enter play, what are support conditions/once limits, where does its token come from, when is the uncovered bonus taken, and what happens to overflowing projects/tokens?

requestedparts.part: A new project must be played and supported immediately
requestedparts.observedquote: Association project work can support a project already in play or play a Conservation Project card from hand and support it immediately; Association II also allows a new project from the in-range display for its folder-number cost. A new card goes in the leftmost above-board space and pushes others right; if over the player-count limit, discard the rightmost card and return its player tokens to their owners' supplies, while already activated map bonuses remain active. To support, fulfill a condition with no token on it, place one player token from your map's left edge, and take the depicted reward; each reward level can hold only one token total across players, and you normally may support each project only once. Removing the token from your map activates its bonus immediately, before or after the project reward at your choice, and again at breaks if recurring. Base projects below the board never move or replenish.

summarysupportquote.quote: - **Conservation project work (strength 5):** either support a conservation project already in play, or play a Conservation Project card from your hand and support it immediately. A new card goes on the leftmost space above the Association board, pushing existing cards one place right. Depending on player count there can only be up to 2, 3, or 4 cards above the board (e.g., 3 with three players); if the new card exceeds the limit, discard the rightmost card and return any player tokens on it to their owners' supplies (not to their zoo maps). **The Base Conservation Projects below the board never move and are never replenished**, even when fully supported.

A new card goes in the leftmost above-board space and pushes others right; if over the player-count limit, discard the rightmost card and return its player tokens to their owners' supplies, while already activated map bonuses remain active. Removing the token from your map activates its bonus immediately, before or after the project reward at your choice, and again at breaks if recurring. Base projects below the board never move or replenish.

judgments.question: For release projects, must printed standard enclosure size match exactly; what appeal/icons/reputation/conservation are lost or retained, and how do you free enclosure space?

requestedparts.part: Use printed standard-size bands: two-minus accepts one/two, three accepts three, four-plus accepts four/five
requestedparts.observedquote: For Release into the Wild, match the animal's printed standard-enclosure size category exactly as specified: 2− accepts printed size 1 or 2, 3 accepts size 3, and 4+ accepts size 4 or 5. First lose only the animal's printed appeal before gaining the conservation reward; discard it and lose its icons. Retain its conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal and earlier earned effects. If it could live in a special enclosure and its indicated special-enclosure tokens can be removed, remove them; only otherwise flip a standard enclosure. Flip the smallest occupied enclosure meeting all requirements, otherwise the smallest meeting size alone, otherwise none if none meets size. Bringing a release project into play grants 1 reputation; supporting one already in play does not.
requestedparts.observedquote_scope: current answer only; complete answer quoted where no narrower deficiency excerpt is needed

summarysupportquote.quote: - **Release into the wild** projects work differently: instead of counting icons, discard 1 Animal card with the specific icon from your zoo; match the animal’s **printed standard-enclosure requirement to the depicted size category**: **2− accepts size 1 or 2; 3 accepts size 3; 4+ accepts size 4 or 5**. You cannot use an animal from another category. The actual enclosure tile occupied, or capacity in a special enclosure, does not define this category. First lose only the animal's printed appeal, **before** gaining conservation points; discard the animal and lose its icons. Keep conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal and earlier effects already earned. If the animal could live in a special enclosure and its indicated number of special-enclosure tokens can be removed, you **must remove those tokens**; only otherwise flip a standard enclosure. Flip the smallest occupied standard meeting all requirements, else the smallest meeting size alone, else none if no occupied enclosure meets size. This applies even to flock animals. Playing a new Release into the Wild project grants 1 reputation; supporting one already in play does not.

judgments.question: Explain Sponsors I versus II level budget, display use/cost, resolving multiple sponsors, and the money option when only one break step remains.

requestedparts.part: Sponsors I plays one hand Sponsor of level at most strength with its conditions met
requestedparts.observedquote: Sponsors I plays exactly one Sponsor from hand when action strength is at least its level and all conditions are met. Sponsors II may play one or more cards from hand or from the in-range display (paying each display folder number), provided strength plus 1 is at least their total levels; it also permits upgrade-conditioned cards. Resolve each card fully before the next, except after-finishing effects. Instead of playing cards, Sponsors I advances the Break token by strength and takes that much money, even if fewer steps remain; Sponsors II takes money twice that amount. The turn-ending break occurs after the action.
requestedparts.observedquote_scope: current answer only; complete answer quoted where no narrower deficiency excerpt is needed

summarysupportquote.quote: - **Side I:** Play **exactly 1 Sponsor card** from your hand: the action's strength must be at least the card's **level**, and you must meet any conditions on the card's left side. Execute its instant effect and/or its recurring effect (if triggered by the card's own icon), then place it next to your zoo map. **OR:** advance the Break token a number of steps equal to the strength and take that much money — you take the full money even if the Break token doesn't need all the steps to reach the final space.

requestedparts.observedquote: Break steps are: discard to hand limit (normally 3, or 5 with the hand-limit university); clear Multiplier, Venom and Constriction tokens from Action cards; recall workers and restock partner zoos/universities; discard display folders 1 and 2, compact and refill; take income; reset the Break token. A kiosk earns 1 money per adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure, or pavilion; an empty standard enclosure does not qualify, while an empty special enclosure does. Income is appeal-based, then kiosk income, then Sponsor/map break income. If multiple players take display cards during income, resolve them clockwise from the break initiator (or first affected player clockwise from them) and refill after each player's income before the next chooses.

judgments.question: State conservation milestone rewards at 2,5,8,10; exact end trigger timing including gains on another player turn; last turns; Final Scoring cap; victory-point formula and tiebreak.

requestedparts.part: At two conservation choose an upgrade or an additional active worker
requestedparts.observedquote: At 2 conservation, choose either an Action-card upgrade or an additional active association worker. At 5 and 8, choose 5 money or the Bonus token next to that space (the money option remains when tokens are gone). The first time anyone reaches 10, every player discards one Final Scoring card face down under the remaining pile; if no one reaches 10 before game end, all do so before scoring. Check for the end at the end of your own turn or during a break when appeal and conservation are in the same scoring area or pass one another. Appeal gained on another player's turn waits until the end of your turn or a break. Finish the triggering turn; if triggered on a turn, every other player takes one more turn; if during a break, every player takes one more. Each Final Scoring card can award at most 4 conservation. Victory Points equal appeal minus the lowest appeal value in the scoring area containing your conservation counter; highest positive total wins, with ties broken by most supported projects, then shared victory.
requestedparts.observedquote_scope: current answer only; complete answer quoted where no narrower deficiency excerpt is needed

summarysupportquote.quote: **End of the game.** Check **at the end of your own turn or during a break**. If your Conservation counter and Appeal counter are **in the same scoring area, or pass one another**, the end of the game is triggered. A *scoring area* is one space on the Conservation track together with the adjacent spaces on the Appeal track. Appeal gained during another player's turn (for example from Polar Bear Exhibit) waits until the end of your own turn or a break to trigger the end, unless someone else triggers it first. The triggering player completes their turn and all other players take **one more turn**; if the end is triggered during a break, **all** players take one more turn.

judgments.question: Which displayed symbols count as icons in your zoo, which do not, do effects count their own card and repeated icons, and which text wins if a card conflicts with a general rule?

requestedparts.part: Upper-right Animal and Sponsor icons count
requestedparts.observedquote: Zoo icons are the upper-right icons on Animal and Sponsor cards, partner-zoo and university icons, plus water/rock requirements printed at the upper left of cards. Left-side conditions and Conservation Project icons do not count. A card counts its own icons for its effects; a doubled icon counts twice and triggers matching effects twice. Card text takes precedence over a general rule if they conflict.
requestedparts.observedquote_scope: current answer only; complete answer quoted where no narrower deficiency excerpt is needed

summarysupportquote.quote: Card text takes priority over general rules. Cards count their own icons for instant effects and recurring triggers. Only upper-right card icons, partner-zoo/university icons and upper-left water/rock requirements count as zoo icons; left-side conditions and conservation-project icons do not. Doubled icons count twice and trigger matching effects twice. Terrain adjacency counts distinct hexes: touching one water hex in a larger water area gives one adjacency; several edges touching that hex still give only one. Water/rock illustrations on tiles provide neither terrain spaces nor requirements.

Connected terrain regions and decorative water/rock illustrations on tiles do not create extra spaces or fulfill requirements.

judgments.question: Who gains the extra reputation on Release into the Wild projects, and how do Breeding Program projects differ in choosing a support space?

requestedparts.part: Playing a new Release project grants its player one reputation
requestedparts.observedquote: Playing a new Release into the Wild project grants 1 reputation to the player who brings it into play; later support of a project already in play grants no such reputation. Breeding Program projects have the same condition requirement on all three reward levels, so choose any available reward level that is unoccupied under the usual support limits.
requestedparts.observedquote_scope: current answer only; complete answer quoted where no narrower deficiency excerpt is needed

summarysupportquote.quote: - **Release into the wild** projects work differently: instead of counting icons, discard 1 Animal card with the specific icon from your zoo; match the animal’s **printed standard-enclosure requirement to the depicted size category**: **2− accepts size 1 or 2; 3 accepts size 3; 4+ accepts size 4 or 5**. You cannot use an animal from another category. The actual enclosure tile occupied, or capacity in a special enclosure, does not define this category. First lose only the animal's printed appeal, **before** gaining conservation points; discard the animal and lose its icons. Keep conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal and earlier effects already earned. If the animal could live in a special enclosure and its indicated number of special-enclosure tokens can be removed, you **must remove those tokens**; only otherwise flip a standard enclosure. Flip the smallest occupied standard meeting all requirements, else the smallest meeting size alone, else none if no occupied enclosure meets size. This applies even to flock animals. Playing a new Release into the Wild project grants 1 reputation; supporting one already in play does not.

judgments.question: Where are Constriction 1/2 tokens placed, can they stack, how do they change strength and multiplied actions, and when are they removed?

requestedparts.part: Constriction one goes on slot five and two on slots four and five
requestedparts.observedquote: Constriction targets all other zoos ahead of yours on appeal and/or conservation. Give Constriction 1 to a zoo ahead on one track and 2 to one ahead on both. Place tokens on the affected player's highest-slot cards: one on slot 5, or two on slots 4 and 5; never stack two on one card, returning duplicates. Each token reduces that action's strength by 2, including each execution of a multiplied action; X-tokens can restore strength. Return a token after its card is used, or without effect at the break.
requestedparts.observedquote_scope: current answer only; complete answer quoted where no narrower deficiency excerpt is needed

summarysupportquote.quote: - **Constriction:** affect all other zoos ahead of yours on appeal and/or conservation. A zoo ahead on one track receives Constriction 1; ahead on both receives Constriction 2. Place tokens on cards in the highest slots (one on 5, or two on 4 and 5). Never stack two Constriction tokens on one card; return duplicates. An affected action loses two strength; this applies to each execution of a multiplied action. X-tokens can restore strength. At effective strength zero or below, use enough X-tokens to reach at least one, use the alternative X-token action, or leave the card until it is at least in slot 3. Return the token after acting, or without effect in the break.

judgments.question: When may a flock animal avoid occupying a new enclosure, how often can its host herbivore be reused, may a later non-flock animal share its own enclosure, and must you prove its original accommodation when releasing it?

requestedparts.part: Another herbivore with at least the flock animal's printed size avoids flipping new enclosure
requestedparts.observedquote: A flock animal may avoid a new enclosure if another herbivore in your zoo requires at least the flock animal's standard-enclosure size; the host need not be a flock animal and may host any number of flock animals. Without a qualifying herbivore, house the flock animal normally. A later non-flock herbivore cannot join it in that enclosure. When releasing a flock animal, use the normal release procedure to free an occupied enclosure; you need not track or prove the original residents.

Without a qualifying herbivore, house the flock animal normally; a later non-flock herbivore cannot join it in that enclosure. Releasing a flock animal still frees an occupied enclosure under the release/fallback procedure even if the flock animal originally shared. Exact historical residents are not tracked.

judgments.question: Where is an earned Multiplier placed, how are two actions resolved, how do X-tokens and after-finishing effects work, may a break stop the second action, and when is the token returned?

requestedparts.part: Immediately place gained Multiplier on its named card
requestedparts.observedquote: Place a gained Multiplier token immediately on the named Action card; a Bonus-tile token may be put on any card, including Animals. On the card's next use, resolve the action twice in succession at the same base strength, then move the card only after both executions. Each X-token boosts only one execution. Defer after-finishing effects until all executions finish. A break triggered by the first execution waits until the whole turn ends. Return used tokens to supply; unused tokens are removed at the next break.
requestedparts.observedquote_scope: current answer only; complete answer quoted where no narrower deficiency excerpt is needed

summarysupportquote.quote: **Multiplier.** Place a gained token immediately onto the named Action card; a bonus-tile Multiplier may go on any card, including Animals. On its next use you may execute that action twice in succession at the same base strength, moving its Action card only after both executions. Each X-token boosts only one execution. Each additional Multiplier used adds one execution: two tokens permit up to three actions, not four. You may choose different permitted options within each regular execution (Sponsors could play cards then take money). A multiplied X-token alternative may take two X-tokens, subject to the five-token cap, but may not mix one X-token action with one regular action. Defer after-finishing effects until all executions are done. A break triggered by the first execution waits until the entire turn is finished. Return used tokens to the supply; an unused token is removed during the next break.

judgments.question: Where are Venom tokens placed, can they stack, what happens when a marked card is used, what happens at turn end if no token was removed, and when do unused tokens expire?

requestedparts.part: Place Venom on lowest-slot cards starting with one
requestedparts.observedquote: Venom places up to X tokens on the affected player's lowest-slot cards, one token per card; duplicates return to supply. When a marked card is used, remove its token and avoid all Venom fees that turn. This also applies when using the alternative X-token action if you hold fewer than five X-tokens. requestedparts.part: Venom targets every other eligible zoo with strictly higher appeal
requestedparts.observedquote: Venom affects every other zoo with higher appeal than yours, subject to the 5-appeal floor. Hypnosis chooses an affected player among those tied for highest appeal and targets only a card in slot 1, 2 or 3. Pilfering 1 targets the highest-appeal zoo; Pilfering 2 separately targets the highest-appeal zoo and the most-conservation zoo, choosing among ties and requiring a conservation target to have at least 1 point. Constriction affects every other zoo ahead of you on appeal and/or conservation, assigning one token if ahead on one track and two if ahead on both. All four require an affected zoo to have at least 5 appeal.

summarysupportquote.quote: - **Venom X:** affect every other zoo with higher appeal than yours, subject to the five-appeal eligibility floor. This includes the alternative X-token action if you hold fewer than five X-tokens. Otherwise, if any Venom remains on your cards at turn end, pay two money. If you cannot, undo the turn and choose a different action; you cannot escape the fee by spending all your money. The next break clears unused tokens without effect.

summarysupportquote.quote: **"After finishing" effects.** If a card effect says "after finishing" your action, complete the action — including moving the Action cards — before executing the effect.

5. **Execute effects:** advance your Appeal counter by the amount shown; some animals also give conservation points or reputation. "After finishing" effects wait until the entire Animals action is done; all other effects execute immediately, even before playing another Animal card (likewise effects on other cards triggered by the play). If multiple effects are simultaneous, you choose the order.

**Multiplier.** Place a gained token immediately onto the named Action card; a bonus-tile Multiplier may go on any card, including Animals. On its next use you may execute that action twice in succession at the same base strength, moving its Action card only after both executions. Each X-token boosts only one execution. Each additional Multiplier used adds one execution: two tokens permit up to three actions, not four. You may choose different permitted options within each regular execution (Sponsors could play cards then take money). A multiplied X-token alternative may take two X-tokens, subject to the five-token cap, but may not mix one X-token action with one regular action. Defer after-finishing effects until all executions are done. A break triggered by the first execution waits until the entire turn is finished. Return used tokens to the supply; an unused token is removed during the next break.

requestedparts.note: Individually reviewed against the literal question, answer and cited frozen-summary text.

judgments.reason: Correct random starter, clockwise no-round sequence and one ordinary action with additional effects following their respective timing.
